transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-31 15:00 UTC · Duration: 42 minutes · Recorded by Fireflies

Summary:
Quick renewal/retainer check-in to confirm Vanguard's planned capacity bump for EU edge activation, discuss latency targets, security questions (KMS/SOC2), and align on commercial tweaks for a 12‑month retainer increment. AE+SE from Redwood: Alex and Priya. Customer side: Jonas (platform), Maya (SRE), Tom (CISO).

Topics:
- EU edge onboarding timeline and IP/network prep
- Reserved retainer increment vs burst credits
- Latency p95 targets and benchmark plan
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency
- Next steps and pricing follow-ups

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick check — can you see my screen? no screen right now, okay perfect. um this is Alex, AE, and Priya's on the call from the infra side.
[00:24] Jonas (Vanguard): yeah all good. Jonas here. thanks Alex. we want to mainly lock down the EU nodes and the retainer top-up numbers so we can plan Q2 deploy.
[00:39] Priya (Redwood SE): hi team, Priya. small caveat, I'll dive into the latency and batching stuff. first question — are you expecting a hard cutover or phased canary into EU?
[00:54] Maya (Vanguard): phased. we want canary for the first 48 hours, then ramp over 3 weeks. our traffic is variable, heavy spikes noon-2pm UTC+1.
[01:15] Alex (Redwood): cool. commercial side — you mentioned a retainer increment of roughly 25% last email, and some burst credits. we can propose a 20% base increase + 30% burst buffer as an option.
[01:35] Jonas (Vanguard): hmm can you explain burst buffer again? like how does it map to cost and SLA?
[01:46] Priya (Redwood SE): sure — burst credits are short-term throughput above reserved capacity. they cost less than permanently reserved nodes but have no SLA for sustained usage. reserved capacity gives you guaranteed throughput and lower unit cost. burst is cheaper per month but not guaranteed.
[02:08] Tom (Vanguard CISO): and from security side we need to understand key management. we use GCP KMS, some HSM-backed keys. will Redwood Private or Dedicated integrate with our KMS?
[02:25] Alex (Redwood): yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS and can integrate HSM-provided keys via our key wrapping flow. small note — sometimes the config steps are manual the first time, Priya can send the runbook.
[02:45] Priya (Redwood SE): i'll send the integration checklist and an allowlist template. also note: audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM — though for Private deployments it's customer controlled.
[03:05] Jonas (Vanguard): perfect. on latency — our product team is strict on p95 under 120ms for short prompts. can you meet that from EU edge?
[03:18] Priya (Redwood SE): based on similar customers, EU edge with Dedicated nodes and prefix caching should hit p95 around 90–110ms for small prompts (<=128 tokens). longer contexts push that up. two caveats: model variant and quantization change tail latency.
[03:40] Maya (Vanguard SRE): when you say prefix caching, can we control TTLs and eviction? we have mixed small and large sessions, and don't want big KV entries evicting working sets.
[03:55] Priya (Redwood SE): yes TTL and size thresholds are configurable per route. we'll propose conservative defaults for the canary. also we recommend warm-up traffic during the canary window to populate caches.
[04:18] Alex (Redwood): regarding benchmarks, i'd like to propose a p95 benchmark test — we'll run with your sample payloads and our canary model. proposed window week of Apr 18, is that okay?
[04:33] Jonas (Vanguard): yes that week works. we'll assemble representative payloads.
[04:41] Tom (Vanguard CISO): also need to confirm retention — do logs or prompts persist in Redwood's hosted control plane? we must know data residency and whether the payloads are stored for analytics.
[04:55] Alex (Redwood): good point. by default request logs for hosted mode are retained for 30 days and trace metadata is available. for Private Dedicated we can limit retention and route logs to your SIEM. we'll share a data residency doc.
[05:10] Maya (Vanguard): ok. can we get SOC2 and ISO certs? procurement wants the attestation pack.
[05:19] Alex (Redwood): yes, we have SOC2 Type II; i'll attach the cert and the compliance pack after the call.
[05:27] Jonas (Vanguard): pricing — can you outline the delta between a pure reserved bump vs hybrid reserved+burst? we need an NPV-ish estimate for finance.
[05:40] Alex (Redwood): i'll send two scenarios: (A) 25% reserved nodes, (B) 15% reserved + 40% burst buffer. we'll include modeled token costs and estimated monthly cost variance.
[05:54] Priya (Redwood SE): technical note — if you expect long-form context heavy sessions (1k+ tokens), reserved gives better predictability. burst credits are good for short spiky inference.
[06:09] Jonas (Vanguard): our main workload is short queries with occasional long transcripts (customer support summarization). seems like hybrid makes sense.
[06:20] Maya (Vanguard): also, what about fallbacks? if EU capacity is constrained do requests route to US region? data residency concerns.
[06:31] Priya (Redwood SE): policy-driven routing possible. you can set strict residency (no cross-region) or best-effort fallback. we recommend best-effort with redaction for non-PII if you can tolerate some routing.
[06:48] Tom (Vanguard CISO): we will not allow fallback for PII-sensitive endpoints. for those we'll need Private or dedicated with strict residency.
[06:59] Alex (Redwood): understood — we'll mark PII routes as strict. that's part of the rollout config.
[07:08] Jonas (Vanguard): on onboarding timeline — if we sign the amendment this week, what's realistic for EU canary spin-up?
[07:20] Priya (Redwood SE): for Dedicated EU nodes, provisioning is typically 7–10 business days once capacity is reserved and network peering is confirmed. Private on-prem can take longer due to infra prep.
[07:36] Maya (Vanguard): 7–10 days is fine. we need IP allowlist and a minimal peering test. can you provide the IP ranges?
[07:47] Priya (Redwood SE): yes — i'll share them in the runbook. note sometimes cloud ranges differ per region, will call that out.
[07:59] Jonas (Vanguard): what about autoscaling? we don't want to constantly overprovision but need headroom in daytime spikes.
[08:10] Priya (Redwood SE): Dedicated supports autoscale policies with warm-up and cooldown windows; you can set a minimal reserve. if latency is critical set a smaller scale step and longer warm-up to avoid oscillation.
[08:27] Alex (Redwood): commercial aside — there is an option for committed 12-month retainer which lowers unit cost by another 12% vs month-to-month. customers typically choose that when they know steady-state QPS.
[08:41] Jonas (Vanguard): finance prefers predictable monthly cost. can we model a 12-month commit with quarterly true-ups?
[08:51] Alex (Redwood): yes — we can add a quarterly reconciliation clause and a right-to-burst for seasonal peaks. we'll draft language.
[09:02] Maya (Vanguard): latency testing detail — can you instrument end-to-end p95 with our synthetic traffic? we'll need trace correlation ids.
[09:12] Priya (Redwood SE): yes we can add x-request-id pass-through and return traces. we'll include example headers. also remember KV cache warming is crucial for p95.
[09:25] Jonas (Vanguard): Priya, one more on quantization — are you doing 4-bit q for EU nodes? we've seen model divergence previously.
[09:35] Priya (Redwood SE): we recommend profile-driven quantization. default EU Dedicated images will be the vetted 4-bit for most models but we'll keep a full-precision fallback. any quality regression gets flagged in Redwood Optimize.
[09:50] Tom (Vanguard CISO): for the SOC2 pack, also need third-party pen test result and incident response SLA. can you provide those?
[09:59] Alex (Redwood): yes — incident response SLA is part of enterprise packs. i'll include the pen test summary; more detailed reports require an NDA which we can start.
[10:12] Jonas (Vanguard): ok good. on timeline — if we get docs and proposal this week, final sign-off by Apr 12 still feasible?
[10:22] Alex (Redwood): that's tight but feasible. we'll prioritize.
[10:27] Maya (Vanguard): small note — our engineers prefer not to rotate IPs during the canary; can you guarantee stable egress IPs?
[10:36] Priya (Redwood SE): for Dedicated we can reserve egress IPs for the cluster; for hosted there is more variability. we'll list options.
[10:47] Jonas (Vanguard): any blockers we haven't surfaced?
[10:50] Alex (Redwood): main open items — exact node count, final decision on reserved vs hybrid, SOC2 docs exchange, KMS contact, and benchmark payloads. we'll summarize and send.
[11:06] Tom (Vanguard CISO): also add SAML/SSO integration for RBAC; we want SCIM for user provisioning.
[11:14] Priya (Redwood SE): supported — we'll attach SAML and SCIM config examples.
[11:22] Alex (Redwood): okay to recap next steps: i'll follow up with pricing scenarios and the compliance pack; Priya sends runbook + IP list; you (Jonas) will send QPS and payloads by Apr 12; Tom will send KMS contact and attestation list by Apr 9.
[11:40] Jonas (Vanguard): sounds good. thanks Alex, Priya.
[11:44] Maya (Vanguard): thanks all.
[11:46] Alex (Redwood): great, we'll target the week of Apr 18 for benchmarking. talk soon.

End of transcript.
